body.objective: Students will be able to name environmental problems.
successCriteria: I can name environmental problems in French
I can describe causes and effects
I can talk about environmental problems in Canada and the world
body.hook: Wildfire smoke, plastic in oceans, melting glaciers: environmental problems are in the news every week. Talking about them in French lets you join a global conversation, because many environmental organizations work in French too.

study.title: Notre planète
study.question: What environmental problems affect our world?
study.passage:
Text (read aloud, written for this lesson):
Notre planète a beaucoup de problèmes. La pollution de l'air vient des voitures et des usines. Il y a trop de déchets et de plastique dans les océans. À cause du changement climatique, les glaciers fondent et il y a plus de feux de forêt. En Alberta, la fumée des feux de forêt peut rendre l'air dangereux pour la santé. Beaucoup d'espèces sont menacées, comme le caribou des bois au Canada.
Cause and effect: à cause de + noun (à cause de la pollution); donc (so); ça cause… (that causes…).
Problem words: la pollution de l'air / de l'eau, le gaspillage (waste of resources), la déforestation, la sécheresse (drought), les inondations (floods).
Activity: cause-and-effect chains: groups link three cards in French, e.g. les voitures → la pollution de l'air → des problèmes de santé.
study.source: Original text written for this lesson.
steps: Use à cause de and donc
discussion: What causes air pollution in the text?
What happens because of climate change?
study.product: Write five cause-and-effect sentences about environmental problems using à cause de and donc.

body.objective: Students will be able to suggest solutions with il faut.
body.iCan: I can suggest solutions with il faut.
successCriteria: I can suggest solutions with il faut, on devrait and the imperative
I can match solutions to problems
I can explain what I personally do for the environment
body.hook: Recognizing problems is the first step; proposing solutions is the next. "Il faut recycler. On devrait prendre l'autobus. Éteignons les lumières !" French gives you several ways to suggest action.

study.title: Des solutions
study.question: How do I suggest solutions to environmental problems?
study.passage:
Solution toolkit (written for this lesson):
Il faut + infinitive: Il faut recycler le plastique. Il ne faut pas gaspiller l'eau.
On devrait + infinitive (we should): On devrait prendre le vélo ou l'autobus.
Nous imperative (let's): Réduisons nos déchets ! Éteignons les lumières ! Plantons des arbres !
The 3 R's: réduire, réutiliser, recycler.
Problem → solution examples: la pollution de l'air → On devrait marcher ou prendre les transports en commun. les déchets → Il faut composter et recycler. le gaspillage d'eau → Il faut prendre des douches plus courtes. les feux de forêt → Il faut respecter les interdictions de feu.
Personal: Moi, je recycle, j'utilise une bouteille réutilisable et je marche à l'école.
Activity: problem-solution matching cards, then each student writes three things they do and two things they will do (futur proche): Je vais composter.
study.source: Original activity written for this lesson.
steps: Learn il faut and on devrait
discussion: Which solution is easiest for you?

What do you already do for the environment?
study.product: Write five problem-solution pairs and a paragraph about what you do and will do for the environment.

examples.title: Il faut
examples.answer: Il faut utiliser des sacs réutilisables.

practice.a: Il ne faut pas gaspiller l'eau.

practice.a: Reducing prevents waste in the first place.

body.objective: Students will be able to create an awareness poster.
body.iCan: I can create an awareness poster.
successCriteria: I can write a catchy slogan in French
I can create an awareness poster with facts and calls to action
I can present my poster persuasively
body.hook: A great awareness poster stops people in their tracks: a bold slogan, a striking image and a clear action. Today you'll design one in French for your school.

study.title: Affiche de sensibilisation
study.question: How do I create a persuasive environmental poster in French?
study.passage:
Poster guide (written for this lesson):
1. Choose a problem relevant to your school or community: waste in the cafeteria, idling cars at pick-up, lights left on, water bottles, wildfire prevention.
2. Slogan: short, catchy, with rhyme or repetition. Examples: "Recycle aujourd'hui pour un meilleur demain !" "Éteins la lumière, sauve la Terre !" "Moins de plastique, plus de vie !"
3. "Le saviez-vous ?" box: one or two facts (from reliable sources, translated simply).
4. Calls to action: three imperatives: Apporte ta bouteille ! Composte tes restes ! Prends le vélo !
5. Image: a clear drawing or symbol.
6. Present (1 minute): explain the problem, the slogan and why your actions matter, using il faut, on devrait and à cause de.
Display posters in the school with the class's permission; vote on the most persuasive.
study.source: Original project written for this lesson.
discussion: Which calls to action are realistic for students?
Which classmate's poster was most persuasive, and why?
study.product: Create and present an environmental awareness poster in French with a slogan, a fact box, three calls to action and an image.
